summary: Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) was a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Shizuoka High School and the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada, later holding posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986) and Reitaku University (~1986–1992).

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui and later served there as professor (~1954–1973), as well as director of the Eastern Institute (~1973–1999).

Hajime Sakurabe (1925–2012) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, obtaining a PhD. He taught at Otani University across multiple roles from 1949 to ~1993, including professor.

Hajime Tanabe (1885–1962) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida, and in Germany under Heinrich Rickert and Martin Heidegger. He served as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku (1686–1769) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711). He also taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui (1882–1963) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, as well as Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Tokyo (1930–1943) and served as Komazawa University president (1941).

Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani (1885–1973) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure. He studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under teachers including Bokusan Nishiari, Kodo Akino, and Sogaku Daiun Harada (1925–1943). He founded Sanbo Zen in 1954.
Halle Elizabeth O'Neal specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kansas under the supervision of Sherry Fowler (attested 2011).

Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh (PhD). He served as head of London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990) and professor of Pali and Buddhism at the University of Toronto (~1966–1969).
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has been affiliated as faculty at Haverford College, with posts attested in 2009 and 2019.

Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his doctorate at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney, later serving as an assistant professor at Yale (1891–1917) and holding a chair at the University of Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt (1930–2017) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf. He later served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965–2000).
Hannu K. Riikonen (1948–) studied at the University of Helsinki (~1967–1984) and later served there as a professor (~1999–2014).

Hans Delbrück (1848–1929) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873). He held academic posts at Frederick William University Berlin (1885) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1885–1921).

Hans Harder (1966–) is an Indologist who studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das. He served as an assistant at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and on an editorial board at Heidelberg (2007).

Hans Hartog (1912–) was an Indology scholar who studied at Tübingen, Bethel, Munich, and Marburg. He completed his PhD at the University of Marburg (1937–1939) under Friedrich Heiler, alongside other teachers including Hanns Oertel.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder (1896–1957) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held posts at Leipzig University (~1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1946), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock (1938–) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed graduate degrees at Northwestern University and Yale University, studying under Warren Cowgill, and served as professor of linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967–2013).
Hans Krahe (1898–1965) was a linguistics scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), Heidelberg University (~1946–1947), and the University of Tübingen (~1947–1965).

Hans Küng (1928–2021) specialized in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, Pontifical Gregorian University (~1948–1955), and Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), later holding a post at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).
